title: Olfactory Epithelium Tissue Harvest, Dissociation, and Nuclei Extraction
author: Benjamin David Webster Belfort

steps.title: Prepare Mouse and Expose Skull
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse and prepare the skull for olfactory epithelium (OE) exposure.

substeps.instruction: Deeply anesthetize the mouse.
Transcardially perfuse with at least 10 mL of ice-cold 1X PBS.
Remove the skin to expose the skull.

steps.title: Expose and Isolate Olfactory Epithelium
steps.instruction: Carefully remove cranial structures to isolate the OE without damaging the tissue.

substeps.instruction: Use fine-tipped forceps to secure the dorsal aspect of the nasal septum at the cribriform plate junction and pull posteriorly to break the main OE free.
Use bone nippers to cut along the frontomaxillary suture and lift the nasal bone off the cribriform plate.
Use bone nippers or rongeurs to remove remaining frontal and premaxillary bone up to the base of the incisor teeth.
Break away the contralateral cranial vault by holding the nasal bone and incisor teeth, allowing the brain and olfactory bulbs to be removed.
Insert forceps into the midline skull incision and separate one hemisphere of the cranial vault to remove orbital bones (frontal, maxillary, and lacrimal).
Cut along the midline of the skull from the foramen magnum through the sagittal and interfrontal sutures to the interorbital incision.
Make a shallow incision from orbit to orbit along the most anterior aspect of the frontal bone (dorsal surface only).
Use fine scissors to make two incisions to break the arches from the squamosal bone bilaterally.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Tubes
steps.instruction: Set up the necessary tubes and buffers on ice.

substeps.instruction: Place one C-tube (Miltenyi Biotec, cat #130-093-237) and two 15 mL conical tubes (Celltreat cat #229491) per sample on ice.
Prepare lysis buffer by adding RNAse inhibitor to pre-made nuclei extraction buffer (Miltenyi Biotec cat #130-128-024) to a final concentration of 0.2 U/µL.
Add 4 mL of 1% BSA to each 15 mL conical tube, vortex briefly, and discard excess to minimize nuclei adhesion.

steps.title: Dissociate Tissue
steps.instruction: Mechanically dissociate the OE samples using the GentleMACS system.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 mL ice-cold lysis buffer to each C-tube for whole OE samples.
Place C-tubes upside-down onto the GentleMACS tissue dissociator (Miltenyi Biotec, cat #130-093-235).
Hold each OE sample over its respective C-tube with #2 forceps and cut into small pieces using fine tip scissors before adding to the tube.
Select the 4C_nuclei_1 program on the dissociator and start the cycle.
Remove C-tubes immediately after cycle completion to avoid over-lysis.

steps.title: Filter and Extract Nuclei
steps.instruction: Filter the homogenized suspension and isolate the nuclei pellet.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate the homogenized suspension from the C-tube (avoiding bone fragments) and filter it through a 70 µm strainer (Miltenyi Biotec, cat #130-110-916) into the first BSA-coated conical tube.
Rinse the strainer with 1 mL of ice-cold 1X PBS.
Gently aspirate and discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of ice-cold 1X PBS by gentle pipetting.
Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4 °C in a swinging-bucket centrifuge.

steps.title: Final Purification and Quantification
steps.instruction: Perform final filtration and quantify the nuclei concentration.

substeps.instruction: Pass the resuspended nuclei through a 30 µm strainer (Miltenyi Biotec, cat #130-110-915) into the second BSA-coated conical tube.
Quantify nuclei concentration using a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter.
Proceed immediately to downstream protocols (with or without FACS).
